---
title: "aggregate() with a formula drops every row that holds an NA"
ref: LEN-13
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: incoherent
controle: [safer-r]
extrait: 'aggregate(y ~ g, data.frame(g = 1:2, y = c(1, NA)), mean)$g'
reponse: '1'
attendu: "one row per site, and the mean height of site A over its two patients"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
visits <- data.frame(
  site = c("A", "A", "B", "C"),
  weight = c(70, NA, 82, NA),
  height = c(170, 180, 175, 160)
)
aggregate(cbind(weight, height) ~ site, data = visits, FUN = mean)
aggregate(visits[c("weight", "height")], by = list(site = visits$site), FUN = mean)
```
:::

## Why

The formula method of `aggregate()` builds its data with `model.frame()`, whose `na.action` is `na.omit`: every row with an `NA` in any of the variables is removed before the computation. The patient of site A without a weight also disappears from the mean height, and site C, which has no weight at all, disappears from the result.

The method without a formula keeps every row and passes the `NA` on to `mean()`, which returns `NA`. Same function, same data, two different answers, and the one from the formula looks complete.

## The remedy

With the formula, keep the rows with `na.action = na.pass`, and say explicitly how `FUN` handles the `NA`. A site without any value then gets `NaN`, the mean of nothing.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
aggregate(
  cbind(weight, height) ~ site,
  data = visits,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  na.action = na.pass
)
```
:::
